post.description: kind local is the admin's explicit opt-in to managing the Docker host Bayplan runs on (D-19): nothing is added at startup. Needs a Docker socket that answers. 409 socket_not_found, engine_unreachable, unsupported_engine (unless allowUnsupported) or local_environment_exists. kind agent creates an environment for hosts that run the Bayplan agent, with its own certificate authority and a join token, and answers install with the token (shown once) and the address the agent dials; 409 public_url_missing when Bayplan has no public URL. 422 invalid_name. The name defaults to the hostname the daemon, or the first agent, reports. Needs environments.create. Audited as environment.added.

delete.description: Needs environments.delete. Stops managing the host. Changes nothing in Docker: its containers, networks and volumes are untouched (D-20). Audited as environment.removed.

post.description: Needs the current password. On success every session of the user ends, this one included, and a new session starts: its cookie is set and its CSRF token returned (D-32, D-34). A wrong current password or a new password that breaks the policy answers 422 with a stable code per field. Attempts are throttled per user and the refusal is 429 rate_limited. Audited as auth.password_changed.
post.summary: Change the signed-in user's own password

get.description: publicUrlLocked is true when the BAYPLAN_PUBLIC_URL environment variable fixes the public URL (D-04).
get.summary: Get the instance name and public URL

patch.description: Only the fields sent are changed. Invalid fields answer 422 with a stable code per field (instance_name_required, instance_name_too_long, invalid_public_url). A different public URL while BAYPLAN_PUBLIC_URL is set answers 409 public_url_locked and changes nothing. A change takes effect at once: the Origin check and the cookie Secure flag use the new public URL from the next request. Each change is audited as settings.updated with the old and new value of every changed field.
patch.summary: Change the instance name or the public URL

post.description: Needs the setup token. Runs once: it creates the admin, assigns the global admin role, stores the instance name and public URL, starts a session and audits setup.completed in one transaction, then consumes the token. A second call answers 409 setup_complete.
post.summary: Create the first admin, store the instance settings and sign in
Check the setup token and return the step 3 defaults
